blocks.text: Jenny called Seth the next morning to confirm the café meeting after school.
Fist-O-Mite returned to Billy’s office through the open window that afternoon. Billy put his notes in his coat pocket, and they left for the café together.
Billy chose an outside café table beneath a permanent green metal roof. A large steel beam supported its front edge between two posts; the rear was bolted to the brick wall.

blocks.alt: Seth waits at the café table.
blocks.text: Seth arrived with Jenny. Billy and Fist-O-Mite were waiting at the table. Seth sat carefully, keeping his hands on his knees.
“Light went down his cable and into the case,” Billy said. Fist hovered above an empty chair. “Water was clear before he brought it. I was there.”
Jenny turned to Seth. “And you were there when the flash hit.” “I didn’t ask for this,” he said. “I don’t even know what I can touch safely.”
She closed her notebook. “I can challenge Daniel’s claim without printing your name. You decide when to tell people about yourself.” Seth finally took his hands off his knees.
Brief warmth touched Seth’s shoulders despite his shaded chair. Jenny tucked back her hair. The sensation passed before he mentioned it.

Daniel had followed them to the café and waited in an alley across the street. He called Luke down from the roof. “They’re going to tell that reporter about us. Bring the glove back and make them leave.”
“And you’ll put me right?”
“Bring it back.” Luke hesitated, then crossed the street.
Fist-O-Mite saw the floating head first. His warning had no joke in it. Blond spikes rose above an iron jaw that clicked like a trap.
“Uncle Daniel says you’re coming back.” Luke’s teeth clicked. “He can’t finish fixing me until I bring you.”
“No,” Fist-O-Mite said.
“Fixing you?” Billy asked. “What did he do?” Luke glanced at Jenny’s camera case. “Stay out of it.” “He’s free to choose,” Billy said, keeping his voice level.
Luke snapped at the empty cuff. Fist-O-Mite darted away, then turned sharply between the café’s roof posts. Luke chased him, his iron teeth closing on empty air.

blocks.alt: Jaws collides with the café roof post while chasing Fist-O-Mite, tearing the steel support apart.
blocks.text: The glove swerved. Luke crashed into a steel post. His iron jaw caught it at full speed, tearing the support apart with a crack. He spun back, dazed. Above Billy and Jenny, the front roof beam dropped.
Seth sprang from his chair and caught the beam with both hands. It stopped inches above them. Its weight dragged him forward; he planted his feet and held on. “Move!”

blocks.alt: Seth catches the falling café roof beam in both palms while Jenny moves toward the doorway behind him.
Fist-O-Mite flies his whole glove body into Jaws’s iron jaw and sends the floating head hurtling away from the café while Seth holds the beam.
blocks.text: Before Luke could recover, Fist-O-Mite turned and flew straight into the side of his jaw. The blow sent the floating head spinning down the street, far beyond the café.

blocks.alt: Seth supports the fallen roof beam while Billy and Jenny move clear of the café entrance.
blocks.text: Billy pulled a chair out of the way. Jenny held the door open, warning everyone inside to stay back. Together they moved the table clear while Seth held the beam above them.

When Billy and Jenny were safe, Seth lowered his end of the beam onto the pavement. The roof settled at an angle, still held by the wall brackets and the remaining post. He stepped back, his palms marked and his hands shaking.
Fist-O-Mite returned to the doorway. Someone inside was calling for help. Billy checked the customers while Jenny caught Seth’s sleeve. “You saved us.” Seth tried to answer, but only nodded.

At the far end of the street, Luke drifted behind a rooftop chimney. The boy had caught the beam. The glove had knocked him clear down the street. He waited until his teeth stopped rattling, then headed for the laboratory.
